Implementation Plan The plan is ready. The fix copies plan.yml's #7477 `pr_not_open` tolerance into implement.yml. When the CI-triage PR is no longer open, implement either closes the issue as superseded, using the trusted classifier from a support checkout made before the main checkout, or hands it to `ai:blocked`. The new tests go into the two test files CI already runs, because `ci.yml` is outside the heal scope. Planning ref: `stable` @ `9e9338339cb3e5310801c9c6cd9b84c0dc84f484` (symbolic `heads/stable`). Integration branch mismatch: `false`. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends plan.yml "Close superseded CI-repair issue (merged PR)" (#7216/#7477) and `scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py classify` Scope-mode justification: The fix copies plan.yml's #7477 handling (lines 227-280: capture resolver stderr, match `outcome=refused reason=pr_not_open$`, downgrade to `::notice::`) into implement.yml's "Resolve integration ref" step. It then hands the issue to one compact step that settles it, using the existing trusted classifier. The optional hardening of the diagnose step (exit 127 when the support scripts were never staged) costs about 6 lines in the same file. It removes a misleading error, so it is included under §6 (correctness before speed). The issue's suggested `agents.d/` fragment is left out because the heal-scope marker on this issue only allows `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, `tests/**` and `changelog.d/*.md` (see Risks). No new script, workflow, env var, scheduler entry, supervisor or DB work is involved. Automation / §20 summary - Changes only existing code: `.github/workflows/implement.yml` and tests. No new script. - Entry point: the existing `implement.yml` `issue_comment` (`/approved`) trigger. There is no new scheduler wiring. - No long-running supervisor. No DB work. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`. ## Files likely to change - `.github/workflows/implement.yml` - `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py` - `tests/test_plan_superseded_merged_pr_workflow.py` - `changelog.d/7540-implement-ci-triage-pr-not-open.md` ## Functions or modules to implement ### 1. implement.yml, step "Resolve integration ref" (`id: refctx`, lines 517-651) - Capture resolver stderr the same way plan.yml does: - set `resolver_err_file="${resolver_stage_root}/resolver.err"`; - add `2>"${resolver_err_file}"` to `bash "${resolver_script}"` inside the existing `integration_branch="$({ ... })" || resolver_rc=$?` capture. Keep that capture string unchanged; tests pin it. - Set `resolver_pr_not_open=true` only when both of these hold: - `resolver_rc -eq 3`; - `grep -Eq 'outcome=refused reason=pr_not_open$' "${resolver_err_file}"`. - Replay stderr before branching: - on `pr_not_open`, use `sed 's/^::error::CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING /::notice::CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING /'`; - otherwise use `cat`. This keeps the existing `CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING ... outcome=routed` log lines. - Insert a new branch `elif [ "${resolver_pr_not_open}" = "true" ]; then`, placed **before** the existing `elif [ "${resolver_rc}" -eq 3 ]; then`. That ordering keeps the audit test's slice (exit-3 branch up to the fallback) free of `GITHUB_OUTPUT`. The new branch: - prints `::notice::CI-triage PR for issue #N is no longer open; implementation is skipped and the issue is handed off.`; - writes `SKIP_IMPLEMENT=true` to `$GITHUB_ENV`; - writes `pr_not_open=true` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; - writes `pr_not_open_pr=` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, parsed from the matched resolver line's `pr=` field with digits only (empty when absent); - writes **no** `ref=` line; - exits 0. - Leave the other paths exactly as they are: - rc 3 with any other reason (including `pr_not_open_extra`) still runs `exit 1`; - rc 75 and rc 2 still fail; - rc 1 keeps its fallback. - Update the comment at lines 606-607 to note the #7477-style exception. ### 2. New step "Resolve workflow support ref for CI-triage PR-not-open hand-off" (`id: pr_not_open_support_ref`) - Placed directly after `refctx`, with `if: steps.refctx.outputs.pr_not_open == 'true'`. - Same pin logic as the "Resolve workflow support ref for duplicate PR notice" step (lines 419-440): - self-repo uses `github.sha`; - a consumer uses the `implement.yml@<40-hex>` pin from `toJSON(job)` passed via `env:`, else `stable`. - Writes the ref to the step output `ref`, not to `GITHUB_ENV`, so no job-env name is added. ### 3. New step "Checkout support source for CI-triage PR-not-open hand-off" (`id: checkout_support_source_pr_not_open`) - `actions/checkout@v5` of `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` at `${{ steps.pr_not_open_support_ref.outputs.ref }}`. - Settings: `path: .codex-workflow-src`, `fetch-depth: 1`, `persist-credentials: false`, `sparse-checkout: scripts`, `continue-on-error: true`. This is the same shape as the heal-report job's checkout at lines 6472-6482. - Same `if:` as step 2. ### 4. New step "Hand off CI-triage issue whose PR is no longer open" (`id: pr_not_open_handoff`) - Same `if:` as step 2. - `env:` entries: - `GH_TOKEN: secrets.GH_PAT`; - `REPO_SLUG: github.repository`; - `HANDOFF_PR: steps.refctx.outputs.pr_not_open_pr`; - `PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR_CHECK_ENABLED: ${{ vars.PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR_CHECK_ENABLED || 'true' }}` (reused switch, no new variable); - `TG_BOT_SECRET`, `TG_CHAT_ID`, `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` exactly as on other steps; - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"`. - The body has no `${{ }}`. It uses `set -uo pipefail`. - Helpers are sourced only from `.codex-workflow-src/scripts/{tg_helpers,label_helpers}.sh`, never from `scripts/`, which does not exist yet because no checkout has happened. `gh_retry` comes from `${GH_API_RETRY_HELPERS}`, falling back to `gh_retry() { "$@"; }`. - Inputs: `ISSUE_META_FILE`, already written by "Precheck approval phase label", and `RUNTIME_DIR` from "Create runtime workspace". - Log lines use the existing contractual prefix: `AI_PHASE_GATE_V1 phase=implement gate=ci_triage_pr_not_open reason= outcome= issue= pr=

`. No new log prefix. Flow: a. **Kill switch.** If the switch is `false|0|no|off` (case-insensitive), skip to (d) with `detail=disabled`. b. **Find the helper.** Use the first regular non-symlink file among: - `$(pwd)/.codex-workflow-src/scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py`; - `$(pwd)/.codex-workflow-src-main/scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py`. If neither exists, go to (d) with `detail=helper_missing`. Otherwise: - read the pipeline login once (`gh api user --jq .login`); - run `python3 -I -B "${helper}" classify --issue-meta-file "${ISSUE_META_FILE}" --repo "${REPO_SLUG}" --pipeline-login "${login}" --out "${RUNTIME_DIR}/implement_pr_not_open.json"`; - read `outcome`, `reason`, `pr`, `final_head_sha` and `comment_body` with the same `field()` one-liner plan.yml uses (lines 976-978); - if the classifier fails, go to (d) with `detail=classifier_failed`. c. **`outcome=superseded`.** - Read the comments once: `gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/${REPO_SLUG}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}/comments?per_page=100"`. This read happens only on this path. The §14 comment above it must say that `ISSUE_COMMENTS_FILE` is not populated until "Fetch issue comments", which comes later. - Deduplicate on `` posted by the pipeline login. - If not already present, post `comment_body` after checking that it contains the marker. - `ensure_label_exists ai:closed`. - `gh issue edit --add-label ai:closed --remove-label ai:awaiting-approval --remove-label ai:planning --remove-label ai:clarification`. - `gh issue close --reason "not planned"`. - Log `reason=superseded outcome=closed label=applied|failed close=done|failed comment=posted|present`. - Telegram: DEBUG on success, WARNING when the label edit or close failed. - If the comment post failed, fall to (d) with `detail=comment_failed`. d. **Any other outcome or failure** (`merged_check_not_passed`, `pr_closed_unmerged`, `not_candidate`, `origin_unverified`, `pr_read_failed`, the (a)/(b) failures, and so on). This is the blocked hand-off: - `ensure_label_exists ai:blocked`. - `gh issue edit --add-label ai:blocked --remove-label ai:awaiting-approval`. - Post a fixed-text comment. It says the CI-triage pull request #`` is no longer open, implementation was not started, the outcome was ``, and the unblock judge decides between closing and re-issuing. Its last line is ``. - Log `reason=blocked_handoff detail= outcome=handed_off label=applied|failed comment=posted|failed`. - Telegram: DEBUG when the label was applied, because the unblock judge handles it automatically. WARNING when the label edit failed; that message says the issue is still `ai:awaiting-approval`. - `detail` is restricted to `[a-z_]` with `tr -cd`. e. **Always exit 0.** Never write `RESTORE_AWAITING_APPROVAL_ON_SKIP=true`. Never reroute or check out a branch; plan's `PLAN_REROUTED_REF` does not reach implement. ### 5. Step "Diagnose post-Codex failure and create fix-up issues" (line 6075). Hardening for the second fault. - At the top of the run body: - resolve `diagnose_support_dir="${IMPLEMENT_STAGED_SUPPORT_RUN_DIR:-scripts}"`; - if `"${diagnose_support_dir}/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh"` is not a file, print `::warning::Diagnose helper not staged (failure before support staging); skipping fix-up diagnosis.` and `exit 0`. - Otherwise the behaviour, including the existing `${IMPLEMENT_STAGED_SUPPORT_RUN_DIR:-scripts}` fallback, is unchanged. - The `handled` output stays unset, so "Comment on issue failure" still posts the generic failure comment. ## Data structures affected - New `refctx` step outputs `pr_not_open` (`true` or unset) and `pr_not_open_pr` (digits or empty). The existing output `ref` is unchanged and is not written on this path. - New step ids
